Fetch ESA WorldCover from Microsoft Planetary Computer

STEP02 queries the inherited AOI directly through the Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC API, reads the selected WorldCover cloud-optimized GeoTIFF, and assigns producer values to the inherited labeled SSU centers. Product identity, date, native support, STAC item, and asset lineage are populated automatically.

Ready. Only labeled SSUs will be sampled in Build002, minimizing network and COG reads while preserving all 3,700 inherited SSUs.

WorldCover retrieval complete

Producer values are loaded as a selectable WorldCover epoch layer. Stay here to review retrieval details, or choose the next view.

Neither choice changes the fetched evidence. The map renders only after you choose Map.

WorldCover 2020 and 2021 use different algorithm versions. Differences between years may reflect algorithm changes as well as land-cover differences.

Comparison gate review

Same place WAITEvaluated from authoritative SSU joins
Time correspondence WAITCompares STEP01 reference dates with producer epoch
Support correspondence WAITCompares 5 m interpretation support with 10 m producer pixel
Vocabulary crosswalk BLOCKReview and lock the WorldCover crosswalk
Producer values remain viewable under PASS, LIMITED, or BLOCK. Paired statistics require same-place PASS and a locked vocabulary crosswalk.

WorldCover epochs and LCMAP annual evidence

LCMAP is expected as annual 30 m LCPRI in EPSG:5070, associated with July 1 of each year. The fetch uses the existing Microsoft Planetary Computer STAC/COG path already proven in this STEP02 lineage. Completed years are retained if a later year fails.

Map Producer and comparison result
Confusion matrix
Rows represent Map User classes when available; columns represent Map Producer classes. When no Map User labels are saved, the matrix retains a “No Map User label” row. Its row total, each Map Producer class column total, and the grand total remain visible. Correspondence metrics remain unavailable until paired Map User records exist.
Map Producer AOI and PSU summaries
Map Producer class legend
Colors follow the harmonized AaP3Km comparison palette used in the map and summaries. Original WorldCover codes remain preserved in producer records.
AOI producer class totals
PSU producer totals
PSUProducer SSUsProducer coverage of 100-SSU designProducer class totals and percentagesMap User labelsPairedProducer-only
Map Producer totals include every WorldCover value fetched for the selected STEP01 SSUs, including producer-only records. Producer coverage is reported against the 100 designed SSUs in each PSU. Paired-comparison metrics remain separate.
AOI fractional-cover scatter graphs
Each point is one PSU. X is the Map User class fraction and Y is the Map Producer class fraction, calculated from the same paired SSUs within that PSU. Producer-only PSUs remain in producer summaries but are not plotted as paired scatter points.
The shaded band is the 95% confidence interval for the fitted mean Map Producer fraction where n≥3 and X variance permits estimation. It is not a prediction interval. A single PSU point remains a valid paired comparison and is plotted and tabulated, but it cannot define a regression line, R², or confidence interval.
Regression statistics
ClassPSUs (n)Slope95% CI slopeIntercept95% CI interceptrR²Residual SEStatus
A single PSU point is retained as a valid paired comparison point. With n=1, regression coefficients, R², and confidence intervals are not estimable. With n=2 and distinct X values, a line is estimable but residual uncertainty and 95% confidence intervals are not. Confidence bands and coefficient intervals require n≥3, nonzero X variance, and residual degrees of freedom.
SSU Map Producer and paired-label review
SSUPSUMap UserMap ProducerStatus
Producer-only rows are valid Map Producer evidence. They remain visible in the SSU table and matrix but are excluded from OA, UA, PA, F1, bias, RMSE, and L1 until a Map User label is available.
PSU fractional-composition comparison
PSUPaired SSUsMap User compositionMap Producer compositionClass-fraction bias
Producer − User		RMSEΔ total (L1)
Fractions use paired labeled SSUs within each PSU. Bias is a class-specific vector (Map Producer minus Map User) because a single mean signed bias across a complete class distribution is necessarily zero. RMSE summarizes class-fraction differences for the PSU. Δ total is the sum of absolute class-fraction differences.
